e.text: A1 hits 10.8%, triple the 3.5% benchmark; asking the Critic how to push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2, A3

critique.summary: A1 leads on every measure: 10.8% reach (P10 10.1%), $735 per point versus the benchmark's $2227, with half of adoption from word of mouth, because the day-5 podcast read and Target drop seed early. Small partners and street teams in the hot zones earn under 1% of adoption each, and the hot zones hold only 1.1–2.0% of the natural audience apiece, so local spend there is the weakest money in every plan.

findings.finding: 10.8% reach (10th–90th 10.1%–11.7%) at $735 per point; the podcast (13.2% credit, $3400), Target (12.2%, $2000) and 14-day social (12.2%, $2520) all pull weight, though Fortnite/Afrobeats lags at 9.0%.
10.0% reach (P10 9.4%) at $789 per point; social over 26 days earns 24.1% for $4680, while the four $300 restaurant partners earn only 0.5–0.9% each.
Weakest plan at 9.4% reach (P10 8.6%) and $839 per point; the three $450 street teams in zones 0 and 3 earn 0.4–0.6% each, and the day-33 team is too late for word of mouth.
3.5% reach at $2227 per point with 30.9% word of mouth; all three plans roughly triple it, so taste-led channels (podcast, Target) are clearly paying off.

changes.change: If any partner is kept, keep only the Waffle House in Forest Park (zone 3, fit 0.787), live from day 0.
changes.why: It is the best-performing partner at 0.9%, sits in the highest-fit zone, and early placement gives word of mouth time to spread.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for A1

plan.headline: Dead Ass host-read plus Target drop: ~3x benchmark reach of natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is to seed early through the places this 55+ Cedric and Steve Harvey crowd already over-indexes on: a host-read on Dead Ass with Khadeen and Devale Ellis (Qloo affinity 0.94), a full-campaign Target co-branded drop (0.95), and two weeks of fit-weighted citywide social. In the simulation, which is built on Qloo taste data and is not a guarantee, this reached 10.8% of the natural audience (range 10.1%–11.7%), about 3.1x the 3.5% benchmark, at $735 per point of reach versus $2,227. Word of mouth drives about half of adoption, so most momentum should build after the first two weeks of seeding, with the strongest pickup in the Country, podcasts and athleisure district and the Pop divas and binge TV district.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 34–28 before launch)
items: Day 34: launch the Target co-branded drop; it runs through launch day ($2,000).
Day 34: start fit-weighted targeted social ads across Atlanta; they run for 14 days ($2,520).
Day 29: run the host-read ad on Dead Ass with Khadeen and Devale Ellis ($3,400).
Give each channel its own tracking link and code.

weeks.label: Week 2 (days 27–21 before launch)
items: Keep social running through day 21, then stop it as planned.
Watch Target and podcast code redemptions by district.

weeks.label: Weeks 3–4 (days 20–7 before launch)
items: Paid seeding is done; let word of mouth carry the campaign.
Keep the Target drop live and check that its on-shelf or online presence is still running.

weeks.label: Launch week (days 6–0)
items: Make sure the Target drop is still live through the night of the show.
Close out spend at $7,920 total and log results against the simulated reach.
